newsitem.title: UK: BAA sets up Heathrow cargo rail study group.
newsitem.headline: BAA sets up Heathrow cargo rail study group.

text.p: BAA Plc has set up a study group to investigate the potential for rail to play a role in air freight operations at London's Heathrow Airport, said head of cargo development Ian Robinson.

He told Reuters that the initial aim of the group was to undertake market research on the subject and to investigate potential demand, rail infrastructure and possible depot locations "and to recommend a way forward".
He added that BAA had nothing to do with a consortium that recently announced plans to develop a 100 million stg rail freight terminal of up to 250 acres near Heathrow.

"We have no involvement in this proposal, submission or development. But if a private venture turns out to be of use to the Heathrow distribution industry, then that's great," he told Reuters, without elaborating.

In a report in the first issue of its new "Cargo Matters" publication, BAA said the study would consider how the air cargo business could benefit from the investment in rail infrastructure and the renaissance in the UK's railways.
"Traditionally, rail was seen as only being suitable for bulky, low-value non time-sensitive goods. But the new players in the rail freight industry are looking at all markets for growth," it noted.
"Bringing them together with air cargo experts could lead to the identification of a whole new market," the report said.

Robinson is chairman of the new study group, which also includes members of the London Cargo Promotional Group (comprising airlines and cargo service providers), BAA rail strategy manager Paul Le Blond and Charles Pennell, of English, Welsh and Scottish Railway.

BAA is currently investing more than 400 million stg in the Heathrow Express Rail link, which will provide 16-minute journey for passengers between the airport and London's Paddington station. It is scheduled for completion in 1998.
